globalContext.primaryTransmissionChannel: Revolving credit card APR spike (21.5%+) and excess savings buffer exhaustion in non-asset owning cohorts.

activeAlerts.headline: 🚨 Bottom 50% Wealth Tier Canary: 8.41% Credit Card Delinquency
activeAlerts.body: While top-level median wealth appears stable, excess savings buffers for the bottom 80% are fully depleted. High APR (21.5%+) revolving credit card debt is driving serious delinquencies to multi-year highs in lower wealth cohorts.

activeAlerts.headline: ⚡ Consumer Credit DSR at 5.87%: Multi-Decade Pressure Point
activeAlerts.body: While fixed-rate mortgages insulate existing homeowners (Mortgage DSR: 3.98%), non-mortgage borrowing obligations (credit cards, auto financing) have surged as a share of disposable income.

activeAlerts.headline: 📉 Personal Savings Rate at 3.9%: Depleted Cash Cushions
activeAlerts.body: US consumers are saving only 3.9% of disposable income, well below the pre-pandemic historical norm (7.4%), signaling that consumer spending relies heavily on debt expansion.
